context: Joe's decision, three options. (a) Make skill-sync-skills public - branch protection becomes available at no cost, but the repo carries personal agent instructions, so review content first. (b) Upgrade the account to GitHub Pro. (c) Accept advisory-only and compensate: the drift becomes visible on main immediately after a bad merge, so a red main is the signal - optionally add the same check to the pre-commit/pre-push path in the canonical checkout so it fails locally before a push, which needs no plan change and is probably the best value. If (c), do (c)'s local hook rather than leaving it purely advisory.
description: skill-sync-skills-lock-invariant-check shipped scripts/verify_lock.py and .github/workflows/verify-lock.yml (PR #13, merged). The workflow works and is green: it passed on the PR and on the push to main at 2026-07-29T12:30:37Z. But it cannot be made a REQUIRED status check, so the invariant is advisory - a PR that ships a stale lock still merges and nothing stops it, which is the exact outcome the item set out to prevent. The cause is the repository plan, not permissions: GET repos/joeharris76/skill-sync-skills/branches/main/protection returns 403 'Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature.' Branch protection is unavailable on a private repo on this plan, so no settings change or token scope will fix it.

preserves.behavior: no personal content is made public without an explicit content review
verify_lock.py behaviour and the existing workflow stay working

verifications.command: test "$(gh run list --repo joeharris76/skill-sync-skills --workflow 'Verify lock' --branch main --limit 1 --json conclusion --jq '.[0].conclusion')" = success
verifications.description: The lock gate still runs and passes on main
Either branch protection is now reachable, or a local hook enforces the check
